summary: Discovery call with NovaTech to understand embeddings + reranking use case. Customer runs a 10M+ document knowledge base, currently using FAISS/Elastic hybrid. Primary concerns: throughput (QPS), latency SLOs for SERP, dimensionality and vector size cost, hybrid BM25 + vector re-rank, and options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/HSM). Redwood AE/SE discussed batch sizing, KV cache behavior, dedicated GPU pools, fallback to smaller models, and a plan to run a benchmark using NovaTech's sample dataset.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Daniel Cho (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Ethan Reyes (NovaTech Head of Search); Priya Singh (NovaTech ML); Liam Carter (NovaTech CTO); Olivia Park (NovaTech Infra)

Summary (auto): quick discovery; talking about embeddings and reranking, current FAISS + Elastic stack, throughput concerns, proof-of-concept next steps.

[00:00:05] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we set aside 45 minutes but we can go 60 if needed, i'm sofia with redwood inference, daniel and maya from our solutions team are here too. can folks do quick intros?
[00:00:18] Ethan: yeah ethan, head of search at novatech, we run the customer knowledge base and search for support and docs, about 10 million documents, we see spikes to 800 QPS during incidents.
[00:00:30] Priya: priya here, ml eng, i own the rerank and embedding pipeline.
[00:00:35] Liam: liam, cto, i'm just listening for infra needs and compliance.
[00:00:40] Olivia: olivia, infra, will be responsible for network/VPC if we go private.
[00:00:45] Daniel: great, thanks, quick high level: is the goal to replace embeddings store or to add a reranker on top?
[00:00:52] Priya: mostly add a reranker — we use BM25 to narrow candidates from ES then FAISS ANN for vector search, then a cross-encoder for final rerank. cost's getting wild with cross-encoder at scale so we're evaluating options: offload embeddings to a managed provider, do smaller dimensional embeddings, or move reranker to more optimized infra.
[00:01:12] Sofia: got it. and what's your target latency for search result pages? p95/p99 numbers?
[00:01:18] Ethan: p95 under 200ms end-to-end is ideal, p99 under 400ms, but currently we're at p95 ~350ms during peak because the cross-encoder is the slow part.
[00:01:28] Daniel: okay, sub-200ms for p95 with a reranker is pretty aggressive if the reranker is a cross-encoder. a common pattern is to keep a fast lightweight reranker (bi-encoder) at 512 or 768 dim for recall, then run cross-encoder only on top-K candidates in a canary or async path.
[00:01:50] [00:01:50] Priya: yeah, we tried 768 dims and it dropped quality a little, but cost saved. curious how redwood's hosted embeddings perf looks and what dims you support out of the box — 512/768/1024/1536?
[00:02:03] Maya: we support common dims; our hosted catalog has 512, 768, 1024 and 1536 variants depending on model family. also we can quantize to int8 paths which can reduce memory and cost for large indexes.
[00:02:18] [00:02:18] Olivia: security question — we need KMS and audit logs, and our legal requires SOC2 and iso certs. private deployment would be preferable if the audit is heavy.
[00:02:28] Sofia: yes we have SOC2 kit and integrations with customer KMS/HSM; for private we offer a VPC private control plane and on-prem packaging. we'll share the SOC2 pack after call.
[00:02:40] Liam: cost — what's the rough unit cost for hosted embeddings vs dedicated reserved capacity?
[00:02:47] Sofia: hosted token/embedding pricing is usage-based; for high QPS workloads a dedicated GPU pool gives predictable throughput and can reduce unit costs. we'll send a sample pricing comparison.
[00:03:00] [00:03:00] Ethan: on the technical side, the big questions are: if we keep FAISS locally, can we still host embeddings with redwood and periodically sync? and how is latency impacted if embedding calls go to hosted service?
[00:03:13] Daniel: yes, that's common. we see two patterns: 1) host embeddings and push vectors to your FAISS instance (you call our embeddings endpoint and write vectors into your index) or 2) use our hosted index/rerank where vectors live on redwood-dedicated infra. pattern 1 keeps your vector DB local and minimizes retrieval latency; pattern 2 simplifies operations and you get Redwood-managed scaling and fallback semantics.
[00:03:36] Priya: for pattern 1, how do you recommend handling throughput — batching? async bulk? we have bursts to 800 QPS; writing vectors for each new document or update is heavy.
[00:03:46] Maya: we recommend batching writes and sharded ingest pipelines; our embeddings endpoint supports high QPS and you can do bulk endpoints with up to N embeddings per request. also we expose throughput guidance and SDKs to manage retries and backpressure.
[00:04:05] [00:04:05] Priya: do you expose per-request cost breakdowns? we want to know per-embedding unit cost as we project spend.
[00:04:11] Sofia: yes, token/embedding breakdowns in console, and you can set quotas and alerts.
[00:04:18] Ethan: about reranker — current cross-encoder is a BERT-like model, slow CPU-bound at 10 QPS per core. would Redwood run the cross-encoder on GPU? and can you do fallback to cheaper models when capacity is low?
[00:04:30] Daniel: we run heavy rerankers on GPU in Dedicated or Private deployments; in Hosted we have autoscaling and fallback policies — you can configure policy to fall back from cross-encoder to bi-encoder or to skip rerank and rely on vector score + BM25 when latency SLOs are at risk.
[00:04:48] Olivia: what's the network hop if embedding calls go hosted and FAISS is in our VPC? e.g., do we pay extra latency due to cloud region egress?
[00:04:57] Maya: if FAISS is in your VPC and you call hosted embeddings, you can colocate in the same region to minimize latency. for private deployment (control plane in your VPC) there's no internet egress. also for Dedicated you can set region pins.
[00:05:12] [00:05:12] Priya: dimensionality tradeoffs — we saw that 1536-dim embeddings gave better rerank quality, but index size and memory cost grew. any guidance?
[00:05:21] Daniel: quality vs cost tradeoff is workload-dependent. for semantic search at scale many teams use 768 as a sweet spot, and then apply a small cross-encoder on top-K. for retrieval-augmented generation or fine-grained intent matching 1536 helps. we can run offline evals against your query set to quantify.
[00:05:38] Ethan: ok; we could try two variants in a bench: 768 bi-encoder + cross-encoder on top-50 vs 1536 but only top-10 cross-encoder.
[00:05:49] Sofia: perfect — that's the kind of A/B we'd run in the pilot. we'll also include quantization options to estimate memory footprint.
[00:05:57] [00:05:57] Olivia: on private, what's the deployment model? air-gapped option? we have some customers with stricter rules.
[00:06:05] Maya: yes, we have an on-prem package and air-gapped installers; for VPC we use a private control plane and customer-managed networking. HSM integrations for key management are supported.
[00:06:15] [00:06:15] Priya: can you talk about KV cache — we depend on prefix caching for chatbot flows, are there similar cache semantics for rerank or embeddings requests?
[00:06:25] Daniel: our runtime has KV cache primarily for autoregressive models, but we also implement request-level caching for embeddings for identical inputs and prefix caching in dialogue contexts. for rerank you can cache cross-encoder outputs for repeating candidate pairs.
[00:06:39] [00:06:39] Ethan: curious about retries/backoff, at 800 QPS we need graceful handling.
[00:06:45] Daniel: autoscaling + burst capacity + traffic shaping. Dedicated gives predictable throughput; Hosted can burst but we recommend reserved capacity for heavy steady workloads.
[00:06:56] Priya: i want to quantify compute cost savings — example: running cross-encoder on our CPUs costs X, what would it look like running on a dedicated GPU pool?
[00:07:05] Sofia: we'll include a sample TCO analysis in the pricing deck — generally GPU-based rerankers are 10-30x faster per inference, with different cost tradeoffs depending on utilization.
[00:07:17] [00:07:17] Olivia: audit logs — we need request level logs for compliance, retention for 1 year. is that supported?
[00:07:23] Maya: yes, we have configurable retention, audit trails, and export hooks to SIEMs. for Private you can keep logs inside your infra.
[00:07:33] [00:07:33] Liam: legal wants to understand data flow diagram — i'd expect a doc showing where embeddings live, who has keys, and where logs go.
[00:07:41] Sofia: we'll send a data flow diagram and the SOC2 pack.
[00:07:45] [00:07:45] Ethan: let's talk architecture options briefly — we want to keep FAISS for ANN because we have custom sharding, but want to outsource embedding generation. i'm worried about request-per-second if we do a synchronous call per user search.
[00:07:58] Daniel: you can do async embedding generation or edge caching. pattern: synchronous for query embeddings (low per-query cost) and async for document embeddings; also warm caches for top queries. plus batching at the network layer.
[00:08:14] Priya: query embedding latency budget is 30-50ms ideally. is that realistic with hosted endpoints?
[00:08:20] Daniel: colocated region hosted endpoints can achieve sub-30ms medians for small models; for larger models expect higher. Dedicated/Private on a GPU with KV optimizations yields the lowest latency.
[00:08:33] [00:08:33] Priya: we have multi-geo users — any advice on geo routing and replication for vector DB and embeddings?
[00:08:40] Maya: replicate hot indexes across regions for read-heavy search; route queries to nearest region for embeddings; Redwood supports region pins and smart routing/fallbacks.
[00:08:52] [00:08:52] Ethan: regarding hybrid search, what's your recommended scoring pipeline? BM25 -> vector ANN -> score combine -> top-K -> cross-encoder rerank?
[00:08:59] Daniel: yes that's the common pattern. score combining heuristics (linear blend, learn-to-rank) vary; we typically do BM25 to get candidates then vector ANN (FAISS) to expand semantic candidates, then a lightweight bi-encoder to re-score, finally cross-encoder for final top-K.
[00:09:16] [00:09:16] Priya: can Redwood host the reranker as a microservice we call, or does it need to be in your runtime?
[00:09:22] Maya: both. you can call our reranker API (hosted) or run it in your private cluster with our runtime. Hosted reranker gives autoscaling and fallback policies.
[00:09:33] [00:09:33] Ethan: let's capture success criteria: improved p95 from 350ms to under 200ms with equal or better relevance; cost per query below our threshold; security/compliance sign-off.
[00:09:45] Sofia: good success criteria — we'll use those for the pilot and benchmark.
[00:09:49] [00:09:49] Priya: next steps i think: we'll share sample dataset and query logs; redwood runs a bench with 3 configs (A: 768 + top50 cross; B: 1536 + top10 cross; C: 768 + int8 quant + bi-encoder only) and report latency, recall precision, and TCO.
[00:10:10] Daniel: yes and we'll include Dedicated vs Hosted baseline numbers and a Private deployment note for compliance.
[00:10:18] [00:10:18] Olivia: i'll coordinate networking with daniel if we need a VPC peering or private connectivity for the benchmark.
[00:10:25] Liam: timeline — legal/infra will need two weeks to review security docs, procurement might take a month after pilot.
[00:10:33] Sofia: ok we'll aim to share docs and pricing within 48 hours and get the benchmark started the following week.
[00:10:40] [00:10:40] Ethan: one more nit: index dimensionality and ANN choice — we use HNSW with FAISS, any tips for memory-accuracy tradeoffs?
[00:10:48] Daniel: HNSW parameters (ef/construction) and quantization can help; we can provide recommended index configs per dimension and expected RAM per million vectors. we'll include example numbers in the bench plan.
[00:11:02] [00:11:02] Priya: are there any case studies of customers similar scale using Redwood for embeddings + rerank?
[00:11:08] Sofia: yes — we have a couple of mid-enterprise search customers; we'll anonymize and send a short case study showing throughput and latency improvements.
[00:11:18] [00:11:18] Ethan: great. that covers most of it. any final questions?
[00:11:24] Priya: just one — for the bench, what metrics will you report? please include p50/p95/p99, recall@k, MRR, cost per query, and memory footprint.
[00:11:35] Daniel: noted. we'll include those metrics.
[00:11:38] Sofia: thanks everyone — quick recap of next steps: share docs/pricing in 48h, nova to send sample dataset and query logs, redwood to stand up bench and run 3 configs, schedule deep-dive in ~2 weeks.
[00:11:52] [00:11:52] Liam: sounds good.
[00:11:55] Olivia: thanks all.
